main_body: A dark gothic weeping-willow-style tree: a drooping brown-black canopy of hanging strands over a short trunk with a flared base
top_band: Canopy top is a mass of dark brown foliage/branch strands starting around rows 3-12 (dark brown with mid-brown highlights). It reads as an organic canopy volume, not a flat band.
evidence: This is an organic tree. The canopy is a rounded mass whose upper part shows the crown top and drooping strands hanging over the trunk and lower canopy. The trunk flares into a base. There is no receding side face and no flat architectural elevation. The canopy overhangs and shades what lies below it, giving a 3/4 read comparable to the reference trees. The kind is organic, so the contract is applied loosely.

style.evidence: The tree uses dark brown tones with a few lighter brown highlights, about 4 steps: near-black brown, dark brown, mid brown, light brown. The outline is a dark brown tint rather than neutral black, and it is used selectively. Texture comes from scattered highlight dots on the strands and trunk, so there are no large flat fills, apart from the trunk base and a dark patch near row 43. It is less rich than the references, which carry 5-6 greens with leaf clumps and a lit canopy. The candidate is darker and has more uniform strands with fewer distinct value steps, so tiles carry fewer colours. It is still plausible next to the reference but reads thinner and more monotone, so it fails.
